problem: Cached Wikidata P625 places the Province of Canada at 60 N, 100 W, outside its historical territory. Post-Confederation federal offices also inherited this jurisdiction from earlier biography clauses.

regional_marker.meaning: Cartographic choice: schematic regional point within the historical province, not a measured centroid, capital or asserted workplace.

capital_policy: Use dated seats. Government relocation years 1844, 1849, 1851, 1855, 1859 and 1865 use the schematic regional marker when only a year is known. Parliamentary session dates may follow the government move. Province jurisdiction is valid only within 1841-1867; no automatic successor is assigned to unreviewed events.

sources.supports: Kingston, Montreal, Toronto and Quebec parliamentary seats and relocation chronology.
Government moved from Toronto to Quebec in autumn 1851, back to Toronto in 1855, then Quebec in summer 1859.
Report on removal of government offices from Quebec to Ottawa in October 1865.
First Ottawa parliamentary sitting in 1866; distinguishes session date from office relocation.
Robert Le Moine was Clerk of the Senate and Clerk of the Parliaments, 1871-1883.
William Pearce Howland, federal Minister of Inland Revenue, 1 July 1867 to 14 July 1868.
